newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israelis shoot 16 Arab in Hebron violence.
newsitem.headline: Israelis shoot 16 Arab in Hebron violence.

text.p: Israeli troops wounded 16 Arabs including five journalists during clashes in Hebron on Sunday as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned Palestinians they would pay dearly if violence continued.
Not even concrete barriers erected overnight by the Israeli army along an invisible line dividing the volatile West Bank city could keep Palestinians and Israelis from clashing.

Palestinians on the PLO-ruled side of the city hurled stones and petrol bombs at soldiers in the Israeli-occupied part of the city. Witnesses said troops responded with rubber-coated metal bullets and live ammunition, wounding 16.

"Our aim is to prevent a deterioration, but if there will be a deterioration on the other side, it will have a very high price," Netanyahu told cabinet ministers according to a statement issued after their weekly meeting.
Hebron has been a scene of almost daily unrest for more than two weeks. Israeli soldiers have wounded scores of Palestinians in protests. Several soldiers have also been hurt.

Israeli soldiers shot and wounded Reuters cameraman Mazen Dana with a rubber-coated metal bullet in his shoulder while he and other journalists were filming an Israeli flag still burning after Palestinian youths had set it ablaze and fled. Dana was at home recovering after being treated at hospital.
A cameraman from Abu Dhabi was hit in the head with a rubber-coated metal bullet and seriously hurt, witnesses said.

Soldiers also shot and wounded a cameraman working for the U.S. television network ABC and one from the Associated Press. An Associated Press photographer was also hit with a rubber-coated metal bullet. On Friday, Reuters photographer Rula Halawani was hit by a rubber bullet in the leg.

"Our attitude right now is clearly to protest to the authorities to allow us to cover the events as we should and not make journalists working in the field a target," Vice-Chairman Conny Mus of the Foreign Press Association told Reuters.

"It is difficult to prove because it is all the time a crazy situation but it is very clear that the soldiers are not very happy with the camera people, especially the Palestinian camera people and I think we can't see this as a coincidence any more...We are talking about six photojournalists shot at and wounded in three days," Mus said.

Palestinians accused the soldiers of imposing a collective punishment by putting up the concrete barriers and isolating the 20,000 Palestinians living on the Israeli-held side from the 80,000 who live under self-rule.
The soldiers are protecting the 400 Jewish settlers who live in the heart of the Israeli-controlled side.

Israel's central area commander responsible for the West Bank, Major-General Uzi Dayan, threatened to take further retaliatory action against Palestinians if they resumed throwing stones and petrol bombs.

Palestinians said Israeli soldiers prevented shopkeepers from opening their stores for a fourth day as punishment for unrest sparked by hostile posters that a Jewish woman put up depicting Islam's Prophet Mohammad as a pig.
Israel apologised for the poster incident and the woman has been charged.

Israel handed over 80 percent of Hebron to the PLO in January under a self-rule deal but kept troops behind to guard the Jewish settlers in the heart of the old city. Peace talks have been in crisis since Netanyahu broke ground on a Jewish settlement four months ago in Arab East Jerusalem.
